data.title: A. Gašpar: Surface finds of the Púchov culture from the central Váh region
data.excerpt: S. Flimmelová came across these finds by chance during trips to two well-known hillforts in the central Váh region and handed them over when an information panel was being installed. A. Gašpar describes the pottery, a well-preserved bronze brooch of the Almgren 237 type and a fragment of a loom weight, and dates the assemblage to the Late La Tène and Early Roman periods.
data.metaTitle: A. Gašpar: Púchov culture finds from the Váh region

children.text: On the occasion of the installation of an information panel, organised by the Hradiská civic association, S. Flimmelová handed over to me the finds listed below. She came across the objects unintentionally during trips to well-known hillforts. The artefacts come from two localities belonging to hillforts already mentioned in the literature, from which, however, the pottery material has not so far been sufficiently published in drawings. The finds are deposited in the Museum of Local History in Povážská Bystrica.

1. Hatné (Povážská Bystrica district), the locality known as Hrádek – or rather south of the rocky elevation on the right bank of the Marikovský potok stream, settlement, surface collection, Late La Tène to Early Roman period, Púchov culture.

Non-selective surface collection at this already known locality on the right bank of the Marikovský potok (Moravčík 1992, 77; Petrovský-Šichman 1965, 68–69) yielded 7 pieces of diagnostic pottery (Fig. 1: 1–7).

The collection was carried out on the adjacent field (today a meadow) to the south of the site of the former quarry, which in the past destroyed the greater part of the roughly 20 m high rocky elevation on which a contemporary hillfort of the Púchov culture once extended (Moravčík 2002, 10; Petrovský-Šichman 1965, 68–69). The recently collected finds add to the information about the occupation of the locality.

children.text: Description of the finds

1. A massive, rolled rim 6 cm wide with three shallow grooves – the rim collar of a large storage vessel (Fig. 1: 1). Internal mouth diameter about 35 cm. The sherd is grey-brown, with mica and medium to very coarse quartz grains (1–5 mm).
2. A fragment with a club-shaped to slightly rolled rim of a barrel-shaped pot (Fig. 1: 5). Mouth diameter 21 cm. The sherd is grey, finely granular, with an admixture of graphite.
3. A fragment with an unprofiled rim of a deeper bowl-shaped vessel with a slightly biconical profile (Fig. 1: 4). Mouth diameter about 22 cm. The sherd is orange-brown, with medium-coarse temper.
4. A rim fragment of a handmade shallow bowl (Fig. 1: 3)? Mouth diameter about 25 cm. The sherd is grey-brown, with mica and coarse quartz grains.
5. A body fragment of a pot with fine and fairly dense vertical to slightly converging combing (Fig. 1: 7). The sherd is grey-black, grey-brown at the fracture, porous, with medium-coarse temper.
6. A body fragment of a pot with fine, in places dense vertical grooves (Fig. 1: 2). The sherd is grey-brown on the outer side and dark grey on the inner, burnished, with medium-coarse temper.
7. A body fragment of a pot with part of an incised wavy line (Fig. 1: 6). The sherd is orange on the outer side and brown on the inner, with coarse temper that protrudes markedly on the surface.

The settlement material obtained from the hinterland of the contemporary hillfort on the rocky elevation can be broadly dated (according to the chronology in Pieta 1982) to the 1st century BC and the beginning of the 1st century AD (phases LT D – B1a). The assemblage also has analogies among the finds from the sacrificial site at Prosné some 3 km away, which is broadly assigned to phase LT D1 (Pieta/Moravčík 1980).
2. Košeca – Nozdrovice (Ilava district), the locality known as Pod Hradišťom, settlement, Late La Tène to Early Roman period, Púchov culture.

The assemblage of finds was collected selectively, i.e. only selected pieces of pottery were picked up (the larger ones, those with decoration…). In all it contained 21 pieces of pottery, of which 18 were diagnostic (Fig. 1: 10–14; 2) – two diagnostic fragments were successfully glued together during processing (Fig. 2: 10) – and 3 non-diagnostic. In addition there was a fragment of a loom weight (Fig. 1: 9), a smaller piece of iron slag (5 × 2 × 1.5 cm) and a well-preserved bronze brooch of the Almgren 237 type, dated to the end of the La Tène period and the Early Roman period (Fig. 1: 8).

The objects were found on the slope below the rampart on the south-western side of the Hradište/Dúbrava hill, dug out of fox burrows (several tunnels) that had evidently disturbed a feature (features). Across the whole western part of the slope below a smaller Púchov-culture fort there extended an extensive contemporary settlement long since mentioned in the literature (Petrovský-Šichman 1965, 55). A great many finds are now known from the locality – brooches and coins recovered by treasure hunters – which testify to the importance of the settlement and of its position in the Váh region in a wider geographical context in the period of the 1st century BC and the 1st century AD (Kolníková 1998; Pieta 2008, 71, 74, fig. 33).
Description of the diagnostic finds

1. A well-preserved bronze brooch with an openwork catch-plate with one circular and two angular openings. The bow is almost straight, with one knob next to the catch-plate and a second knob on the upper part of the bow, at the start of the trapezoidal, convex head. The chord is external, held in a hook on the head. The spring is bilateral, asymmetrical, 3:4. Length of the brooch: 10.2 cm, height: 2.8 cm (Fig. 1: 8).

2. A fragment of the upper part of a pyramidal loom weight (4.5 × 4.5 × 6.5 cm). Part of the perforation survives on the inner fracture (Fig. 1: 9). On the surface it is orange-brown, at the fracture grey to dark orange; it is made of fine levigated clay.

3. A fragment of a rounded, everted rim of a barrel-shaped pot, with a small surviving fragment of combed decoration (Fig. 1: 13). Mouth diameter about 30 cm. The sherd is orange-brown with mica and medium-coarse quartz grains.

4. A fragment of a slightly thickened rim of a pot with a shallow groove between the rim and the shoulder, and with combed decoration (Fig. 1: 12). Mouth diameter 19 cm. The sherd is grey-brown with mica and coarser quartz grains.

5. A fragment of a horizontally cut, slightly inturned rim of a pot with two circumferential grooves on the shoulder of the vessel (Fig. 1: 10). Mouth diameter 20 cm. The sherd is grey-brown on the outer side, grey-brown to brown-black on the inner and dark orange at the fracture, with coarse temper.

6. A fragment of a simple rim of a handmade bowl-shaped vessel with an incised line on the neck and vertically incised lines on the body (Fig. 1: 14). Mouth diameter 28 cm. The sherd is brown-black with coarse to very coarse temper, predominantly quartz.
7. A fragment of a simple inturned rim of a handmade barrel-shaped vessel (Fig. 1: 11). Mouth diameter 18 cm. The sherd is grey-brown in colour, with coarse to very coarse temper.

8. A fragment from the junction of the rim and the shoulder of a pot with a shallow groove (Fig. 2: 9). The sherd is light brown on the outer side and brown-black on the inner, with mica and coarser quartz grains.
9. A body fragment of a pot with two vertically incised lines (Fig. 2: 6). The sherd is grey-brown on the outer side and grey on the inner, with mica and medium-coarse temper.

children.text: 10. A larger body fragment of a handmade pot (2 pieces glued together) with vertically incised lines (“disintegrated” combing; Fig. 2: 10). The sherd is red-brown on the outer side and brown on the inner, with coarse quartz grains.

11. A body fragment of a handmade pot with vertically incised lines (Fig. 2: 2). The sherd is dark orange on the outer side and black on the inner (a “pitch-like” coating), with coarse and very coarse quartz grains.
12. A body fragment of a handmade pot with vertically incised lines (Fig. 2: 8). The sherd is dark brown, with coarse quartz grains.
13. A fragment of the shoulder and body of a pot with dense combing (Fig. 2: 7). The sherd is orange-brown on the outer side and brown-black on the inner, with mica and coarse quartz grains.
14. A body fragment of a pot with dense combing (Fig. 2: 4). The sherd is dark brown on the outer side and brown on the inner, with mica and coarse quartz grains.
15. A smaller body fragment of a pot with dense combing (Fig. 2: 5). The sherd is orange on the outer side and dark brown on the inner, with mica and coarse quartz grains.
16. A smaller body fragment of a pot with very dense combing (Fig. 2: 3). The sherd is dark brown on the outer side and brown-black on the inner, with coarse quartz grains.
17. A larger body fragment of a storage vessel; fine lines are discernible on the outer side – textile impressions? (Fig. 2: 1). The sherd is dark brown, with mica and medium-coarse quartz grains.

18. A base fragment of a smaller wheel-thrown bottle-shaped vessel with traces of incised decoration (Fig. 2: 11). Base diameter 4 cm. The sherd is dark grey on the surface, dark brown at the fracture, finely burnished, made of finely levigated clay.

19. A base fragment of a storage vessel (Fig. 2: 12). Base diameter 33 cm. The sherd is grey-brown on the outer side, black on the inner and on both sides of the base (a “pitch-like” coating), with coarse and very coarse quartz grains.

The finds can be broadly dated, on the basis of the brooch that was found but also of the wider range of pottery material, to the Late La Tène and Early Roman periods. In conclusion it should be mentioned that the locality is being continually damaged by metal detectorists, and more frequent inspections of it would therefore perhaps be advisable.
SUMMARY:

SURFACE FINDS OF THE PÚCHOV CULTURE FROM THE CENTRAL VÁH REGION. The finds were made by S. Flimmelová unintentionally during trips to well-known hillforts. They come from two localities belonging to hillforts already mentioned in the literature. The assemblage is deposited in the Museum of Local History in Povážská Bystrica.

1. Hatné (Povážská Bystrica district), the locality known as Hrádek – or rather south of the rocky elevation on the right bank of the Marikovský potok, settlement, surface collection, Late La Tène period, Púchov culture.

Non-selective surface collection yielded 7 pieces of diagnostic pottery (Fig. 1: 1–7). They were found to the south of the rocky elevation on which a contemporary hillfort of the Púchov culture once extended (Moravčík 2002, 10). The assemblage can be broadly dated to the 1st century BC and the beginning of the 1st century AD.
Nozdrovice (Ilava district), the locality known as Pod Hradišťom, settlement, Late La Tène to Early Roman period, Púchov culture.

The assemblage was collected selectively. Besides a wider range of pottery material (Fig. 1: 10–14; 2) it contained a fragment of a loom weight (Fig. 1: 9), a smaller piece of iron slag (5 × 2 × 1.5 cm) and a well-preserved bronze brooch of the Almgren 237 type (Fig. 1: 8). The finds were made on the slope below the rampart on the south-western side of the Hradište/Dúbrava hill, dug out of fox burrows (several tunnels). A great many finds are now known from the locality – brooches and coins recovered by treasure hunters – which testify to the importance of the settlement and of its position in the Váh region in the period of the 1st century BC and the 1st century AD (Kolníková 1998; Pieta 2008, 71, 74, fig. 33).
